C-PREFERENCES-SYNC-FULL-SCREEN.Summary: Display Preferences and Sync as full-screen destinations with the same terminal mode, border styling, and outer spacing as the main exercises and sets view.
C-PREFERENCES-SYNC-FULL-SCREEN.Problem: Preferences and Sync currently return views without alternate-screen mode and render content-sized frames, so entering them does not preserve the main view's full-screen presentation.

Goals.Goal: Keep Preferences and Sync in the alternate terminal screen throughout navigation from and back to the main view.
Expand each secondary screen's single panel to the available terminal width and height, accounting for the main view's outer spacing and any return hint.
Resize both screens to fit the current terminal dimensions while retaining their existing content and actions.

Constraints.Constraint: Reuse the main view's normal border, active-panel color, panel padding, and one-row vertical and two-column horizontal outer spacing where dimensions allow.
Preserve p and s entry shortcuts, g/k/l preference selection and persistence, Sync store/load dispatch and status messages, and q/esc return navigation.
Returning to records retains the existing active panel, selections, pagination, and scroll state, subject to existing resizing and preference-update behavior.
Keep output within terminal bounds on compact and tiny sizes; render gracefully when there is insufficient room for a complete frame.
Preserve existing workspace changes. Planning must account for overlapping ownership in the active C-DOMAIN-MODEL-CONSTRUCTORS change before execution.
Follow repository Go formatting and semantic markup conventions; update durable graph and verification state only through the approved change lifecycle.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Add a new Settings destination or rename the existing Preferences and Sync screens.
Add preferences, implement a remote provider, or change persistence, domain models, schema, or synchronization behavior.
Redesign the exercises and sets view, help screen, dialogs, or keyboard interaction model.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Opening either Preferences with p or Sync with s returns a view with alternate-screen mode enabled; returning with q or esc keeps the main view in alternate-screen mode.

At ordinary terminal sizes, including 100 columns by 40 rows, each secondary screen has one panel whose border expands across the usable width and height with the main view's outer spacing, instead of fitting only its text.

Both panels use the main view's normal border, active-panel color, and internal padding. Existing screen titles, actions, status messages, and a return hint remain visible when sufficient space exists.
Window-size events recompute the layout for both screens. Output never exceeds the supplied width or height at wide, compact, and tiny terminal sizes.
Preference selection still persists and updates displayed weight units; Sync store/load actions and unavailable/error/success messages retain their existing behavior.
Navigation tests demonstrate that entering and leaving either screen preserves the existing records browsing state and shortcuts.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Rendering assertions check alternate-screen mode on entry and return, panel width and height, consistent border and spacing, and bounds after resizing at wide, compact, and tiny sizes.
Interaction coverage checks preference persistence, Sync action dispatch and status rendering, q/esc return navigation, and retained records state.
Existing tests pass without setting UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 during validation. Any intentionally changed snapshots receive explicit review.
GRACE validation checks the specification against the current baseline before implementation; target and final evidence are defined later in the approved plan.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user confirmed that settings means the existing Sync screen, opened with s.
Full screen means a single expanded panel for each destination, matching the main view's terminal presentation and spacing.
